title: Pool and distributor wiring is not cross-checked, and rewardToken may equal stakingToken
summary: setDistributor is one-shot and does not check that the distributor's pool is this pool or that its reward token differs from stakingToken. The RewardDistributor constructor takes pool and rewardToken without validation. A wrong value is permanent because setDistributor cannot be called twice. Nothing stops rewardToken and stakingToken being the same token, which the accounting does not anticipate.
impact: A deployment mistake bricks the pool (setDistributor cannot be repeated) or ties the distributor to the wrong pool. No attacker-triggerable loss was found; this is hardening.
preconditions: The deployer sets a mismatched distributor, or deploys the distributor with a wrong pool or reward token

evidence.description: setDistributor stores any address once; it does not call distributor.pool() or check the reward token.

verification.reason: Raised by the verifier as a new, unverified observation; impact depends on deployment values not in the repository.

remediation: In setDistributor require distributor_.pool() == address(this) and address(distributor_.rewardToken()) != address(stakingToken). Reject the zero address in the RewardDistributor constructor.
regression_test: setDistributor with a distributor built for another pool reverts; setDistributor with matching wiring succeeds once.
limitations: Deployment script and token addresses are not part of the reviewed scope.
The verifier did not examine this one in depth.
